guides.title: Theorem A
guides.source:
def TheoremAStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Type u) [NonUnitalCommRing A] [Module ℂ A]
    [IsScalarTower ℂ A A] [SMulCommClass ℂ A A]
    [UniformSpace A] [IsUniformAddGroup A] [T2Space A] [CompleteSpace A],
    IsLocallyMultiplicativelyConvex A →
    ∀ χ : Character A, BoundedOnBoundedSets A (fun a => χ.val a)
guides.introduction: Read the hypotheses from left to right, then open the two definitions in the final line to see the character and the bound.

steps.heading: Any size of algebra
steps.reading: Let u be an arbitrary universe level.
steps.mathMeaning: The underlying type A may lie in any universe. This is Lean's organisation of types by size; it imposes no finiteness or countability condition on A.
steps.role: Keeps the theorem general across universe levels.

steps.heading: Name the proposition
steps.reading: Define TheoremAStatement to be the following proposition.
steps.mathMeaning: This line gives the mathematical statement a name. The declaration theoremA in TheoremA.lean proves exactly this proposition.
steps.role: Separates the statement from its proof.

steps.heading: A commutative complex algebra
steps.reading: For every type A with a commutative associative ring structure, possibly without an identity, and a complex vector-space structure.
steps.mathMeaning: A has addition, additive inverses, and associative commutative multiplication distributing over addition. Module ℂ A makes it a complex vector space. NonUnital means an identity is not required; algebras that have an identity are included.
steps.role: Specifies the algebraic setting without requiring a unit.

steps.source: [IsScalarTower ℂ A A] [SMulCommClass ℂ A A]
steps.heading: Complex bilinearity
steps.reading: Complex scalar multiplication is compatible with multiplication in A.
steps.mathMeaning: These conditions give (c • x) * y = c • (x * y) and x * (c • y) = c • (x * y). Together with the preceding laws, multiplication is complex bilinear.
steps.role: Makes the ring and vector-space structures one complex algebra.

steps.heading: A topology with a uniformity
steps.reading: A carries a uniform space structure.
steps.mathMeaning: A uniformity describes when two points are uniformly close and determines a topology. The topology used by all the later conditions is this same topology.
steps.role: Provides the setting for Cauchy behaviour and completeness.

steps.heading: The additive uniformity
steps.reading: The uniformity is compatible with the additive group.
steps.mathMeaning: The subtraction map (x, y) ↦ x − y is uniformly continuous. Thus the uniform structure agrees with the usual additive-group notion of closeness, measured by differences near zero.
steps.role: Ensures completeness concerns the algebra's additive topology.

steps.heading: Hausdorff separation
steps.reading: The topology on A is Hausdorff.
steps.mathMeaning: Distinct points can be separated by disjoint open neighbourhoods. In particular, a nontrivial convergent filter has at most one limit.
steps.role: Rules out ambiguity of limits.

steps.heading: Completeness
steps.reading: A is complete for its uniformity.
steps.mathMeaning: Every Cauchy filter converges in A. This formulation covers spaces without a metric; it is not limited to Cauchy sequences.
steps.role: Allows convergent series and compatible limits to remain in A.

steps.heading: A topology from submultiplicative seminorms
steps.reading: Assume the topology is generated by a family of submultiplicative complex seminorms.
steps.mathMeaning: The family may be uncountable. No single norm, countable defining sequence, or metrisability is required.
steps.role: Connects multiplication with the topology.

steps.heading: Every algebraic character
steps.reading: For every character χ on A.
steps.mathMeaning: A character is a nonzero complex-linear multiplicative map to ℂ. There is no continuity or boundedness hypothesis on χ.
steps.role: Makes boundedness the theorem's conclusion, not a condition on the character.

steps.heading: A bound on every bounded set
steps.reading: The function a ↦ χ(a) is bounded on every bounded subset of A.
steps.mathMeaning: After χ and a bounded set B have been fixed, there is a finite nonnegative real C with |χ(a)| ≤ C for every a in B. The number C may depend on χ and B. The expression χ.val selects the homomorphism carried by the nonzero-character subtype.
steps.role: States the precise conclusion of Theorem A.

links.label: Why χ has a val field

notes: The square brackets are Lean's notation for implicit structures and compatibility conditions. They are still hypotheses quantified over by the theorem.
A may be the zero algebra. In that case there is no nonzero character, so the character clause is vacuous.
The result is boundedness on bounded sets. The continuity corollary for the metrisable case is separate.

guides.title: Character
guides.introduction: A character combines an algebraic homomorphism with the condition that it is not the zero map.

steps.heading: Name the definition
steps.reading: Introduce Character as an abbreviation.
steps.mathMeaning: The expression on the right describes the nonzero algebraic homomorphisms. The abbreviation imposes exactly those conditions.
steps.role: Theorem A uses this definition with the same algebra A throughout.

steps.heading: A complex algebra homomorphism
steps.reading: A nonunital complex algebra homomorphism from A to ℂ.
steps.mathMeaning: The map preserves zero, addition, complex scalar multiplication, and multiplication: χ(xy) = χ(x)χ(y). The notation includes no topology or continuity condition. It makes sense even when A has no identity.
steps.role: Records exactly the algebraic laws of a character.

steps.heading: Exclude the zero map
steps.reading: Take those homomorphisms χ for which χ is not zero.
steps.mathMeaning: The braces with // form a subtype: an element consists of a homomorphism together with a proof that it is not the zero homomorphism. Thus χ is nonzero at some element of A. The notation χ.val recovers its homomorphism.
steps.role: Matches the manuscript's convention that a character is nonzero.

notes: The zero map would itself be bounded on every set, but it is excluded from the definition of character.
For an algebra with an identity, a nonzero multiplicative complex-linear map to ℂ necessarily sends the identity to 1. Requiring a unit is unnecessary here.

guides.title: IsSubmultiplicative
guides.source:
def IsSubmultiplicative (p : Seminorm ℂ A) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : A, p (x * y) ≤ p x * p y
guides.introduction: Submultiplicativity is the additional inequality that links a seminorm to multiplication.

steps.source: def IsSubmultiplicative (p : Seminorm ℂ A) : Prop :=
steps.heading: Name the definition
steps.reading: Define a proposition with this name and these parameters.
steps.mathMeaning: The following conditions say when the proposition holds. Writing the definition does not prove that an arbitrary algebra or map satisfies it.
steps.role: Theorem A uses this definition with the same algebra A throughout.

steps.heading: Begin with a complex seminorm
steps.reading: Let p be a seminorm on the complex vector space A.
steps.mathMeaning: A seminorm is a nonnegative real-valued function satisfying p(x + y) ≤ p(x) + p(y) and p(c • x) = |c|p(x). It may vanish at nonzero elements.
steps.role: Measures the size of elements without requiring a norm.

steps.heading: Every pair of elements
steps.reading: For all x and y in A.
steps.mathMeaning: The inequality must hold throughout the algebra, with the same seminorm p.
steps.role: Makes the control of multiplication global.

steps.source: p (x * y) ≤ p x * p y
steps.heading: Control the size of a product
steps.reading: p of x times y is at most p of x multiplied by p of y.
steps.mathMeaning: Multiplying two elements cannot increase their p-size beyond this product. Repeated use gives p(x^m) ≤ p(x)^m for positive integers m. There is no normalisation such as p(1) = 1.
steps.role: Supports estimates for products and power-series substitution.

links.label: Apply this to every defining seminorm

notes: The zero seminorm is allowed. Hausdorffness is required of the topology generated by the whole family, not of each seminorm separately.

guides.title: IsLocallyMultiplicativelyConvex
guides.source:
def IsLocallyMultiplicativelyConvex : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Set (Seminorm ℂ A),
    (∀ p ∈ P, IsSubmultiplicative A p) ∧
    WithSeminorms (fun p : P => p.val)
guides.introduction: The existing topology must be exactly the topology generated by a suitable family of submultiplicative seminorms.

steps.heading: Name the definition
steps.reading: Define a proposition with this name and these parameters.
steps.mathMeaning: The following conditions say when the proposition holds. Writing the definition does not prove that an arbitrary algebra or map satisfies it.
steps.role: Theorem A uses this definition with the same algebra A throughout.

steps.heading: Choose a defining family
steps.reading: There exists a set P of complex seminorms on A.
steps.mathMeaning: The family is arbitrary: it may be finite, countable, or uncountable. This definition does not require P to be nonempty.
steps.role: Describes the topology without choosing a metric or a single norm.

links.label: Where the theorem uses this condition

steps.heading: Control multiplication in every seminorm
steps.reading: Every p in the chosen family is submultiplicative.
steps.mathMeaning: For each p in P and every x,y in A, p(xy) ≤ p(x)p(y). The same family therefore describes both the topology and the estimates for multiplication.
steps.role: Connects the locally convex topology to the algebra product.

steps.heading: Both conditions for one family
steps.reading: The seminorms are submultiplicative, and they generate the topology.
steps.mathMeaning: The same family P must satisfy both requirements. Two unrelated families would not give this definition.
steps.role: Joins the multiplication condition to the topological condition.

steps.heading: Generate exactly this topology
steps.reading: The given topology is the topology generated by the seminorms in P.
steps.mathMeaning: Finite intersections of sets p(x) < ε, with p in P and ε > 0, form a neighbourhood basis at zero. WithSeminorms requires equality with the existing topology, not merely continuity of the individual seminorms.
steps.role: Ensures the seminorm estimates concern the same topology as completeness and boundedness.

steps.heading: Use the members of P as indices
steps.reading: To a member p of P, associate its underlying seminorm p.val.
steps.mathMeaning: Lean treats membership in P as a subtype. A member carries a seminorm together with proof that it belongs to P; p.val selects the seminorm.
steps.role: Turns the set P into the family expected by WithSeminorms.

links.label: The same subtype notation for characters

notes: Because the topology comes from complex seminorms, scalar multiplication has the usual continuity. Submultiplicativity gives continuity of multiplication.
Hausdorffness is a separate hypothesis of Theorem A. Together with WithSeminorms it means the family separates distinct elements.
An empty family generates the indiscrete topology. Under the theorem's Hausdorff hypothesis this can occur only for a one-element algebra.

guides.title: BoundedOnBoundedSets
guides.introduction: For each bounded subset, the character has one finite bound valid at every point of that subset.

steps.heading: Name the definition
steps.reading: Define a proposition with this name and these parameters.
steps.mathMeaning: The following conditions say when the proposition holds. Writing the definition does not prove that an arbitrary algebra or map satisfies it.
steps.role: Theorem A uses this definition with the same algebra A throughout.

steps.heading: A property of a function
steps.reading: Let χ be a function from A to ℂ.
steps.mathMeaning: The boundedness property itself is defined for any function. Theorem A applies it to the underlying function of an algebraic character.
steps.role: Keeps the conclusion separate from the homomorphism laws.

links.label: The character used in Theorem A

steps.heading: Every subset under consideration
steps.reading: For every subset B of A.
steps.mathMeaning: B is chosen after A and χ. It can be finite or infinite, and it can be empty.
steps.role: Requires the property on all bounded subsets, not just on sequences.

steps.heading: Bounded in the locally convex sense
steps.reading: If B is von Neumann bounded over ℂ.
steps.mathMeaning: Every neighbourhood of zero absorbs B: its complex scalar multiples contain B whenever the scalar has sufficiently large modulus. For a topology generated by seminorms, this is equivalent to each defining seminorm being bounded on B, with a bound that may depend on the seminorm.
steps.role: Uses the intrinsic notion of boundedness even without a norm or metric.

steps.heading: Choose a finite bound
steps.reading: There exists a nonnegative real number C.
steps.mathMeaning: C is chosen after the character and the set B. It may depend on both, but it must be one finite real number for the whole of B.
steps.role: States the correct dependence of the bound.

steps.heading: One bound at every point
steps.reading: For every a in B, the modulus of χ(a) is at most C.
steps.mathMeaning: The complex image χ(B) lies in the closed disk of radius C centred at zero. The bound is uniform over B; it is not chosen separately for each a.
steps.role: Expresses boundedness of the character's image.

notes: For the empty set, C = 0 works.
No bound is required on the whole algebra unless the whole algebra is itself a bounded set.
This conclusion alone is not phrased as continuity. The metrisable continuity corollary is a separate consequence.

character.name: Character
character.title: Algebraic character
character.meaning:
A character is a nonzero complex-linear multiplicative map \chi\colon A\to\mathbb C.

\chi(xy)=\chi(x)\chi(y),\qquad\chi(cx+dy)=c\chi(x)+d\chi(y).

Continuity is not part of this definition.
character.provenance: Project abbreviation using Mathlib’s nonunital algebra homomorphisms.

submultiplicative.name: IsSubmultiplicative
submultiplicative.title: Submultiplicative seminorm
submultiplicative.meaning:
A complex seminorm p is submultiplicative when

p(xy)\leq p(x)p(y)\qquad(x,y\in A).

No normalisation at the identity is required.
submultiplicative.provenance: Project definition, using Mathlib’s complex seminorms.

locally-multiplicatively-convex.name: IsLocallyMultiplicativelyConvex
locally-multiplicatively-convex.title: Local multiplicative convexity
locally-multiplicatively-convex.meaning:
The topology of A is generated by a family of submultiplicative complex seminorms.

The family may be uncountable. The topology generated by it is the same topology used in the completeness and Hausdorff hypotheses.

bounded-on-bounded-sets.name: BoundedOnBoundedSets
bounded-on-bounded-sets.title: Boundedness on bounded sets
bounded-on-bounded-sets.meaning:
Every bounded subset B has a finite bound on the moduli of its images:

\exists C\geq0\quad\forall a\in B,\quad|\chi(a)|\leq C.

The same C works for all a\in B; it may depend on \chi and B.
bounded-on-bounded-sets.provenance: Project definition, using Mathlib’s von Neumann boundedness.

proof.title: The checked theorem
proof.reading: Theorem A is proved at every universe level u.
proof.mathMeaning: The declaration has the exact type TheoremAStatement.{u}. Its proof uses the project's proved flag-approximation theorem and the established algebraic reduction.
proof.role: Connects the named proposition to the verified proof.

verification.scope: The integrated check verified the exact universe-polymorphic theorem, with no further mathematical hypotheses, no unexpected axioms, and no unsafe project declarations. It freshly checked 138 added mathematical modules and three combined checks, reusing 113 unchanged project modules and the pinned external libraries.
